officialTitle: Adjuvant Olaparib for Patients with BRCA1- or BRCA2-Mutated Breast Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 1836 patients underwent randomization.
design.notes: 1:1 randomisation to 1 year of oral olaparib or placebo after local treatment and neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. Endocrine therapy given concurrently for HR+ disease.

sponsor: National Cancer Institute / AstraZeneca (Breast International Group, NRG Oncology)
clinicalQuestion: Does 1 year of adjuvant olaparib improve invasive disease-free survival in high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants?

pico.population: HER2-negative early breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and high-risk clinicopathological features after local treatment and (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: IDFS. Secondary: distant DFS, OS, safety, quality of life

publications.title: Adjuvant Olaparib for Patients with BRCA1- or BRCA2-Mutated Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary (first interim) analysis

publications.title: Overall survival in the OlympiA phase III trial of adjuvant olaparib in patients with germline pathogenic variants in BRCA1/2 and high-risk, early breast cancer.
publications.label: Second interim OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: At a prespecified event-driven interim analysis with a median follow-up of 2.5 years, the 3-year invasive disease-free survival was 85.9% in the olaparib group and 77.1% in the placebo group (difference, 8.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.5 to 13.0; hazard ratio for invasive disease or death, 0.58; 99.5% CI, 0.41 to 0.82; P<0.001).

The 3-year distant disease-free survival was 87.5% in the olaparib group and 80.4% in the placebo group (difference, 7.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 3.0 to 11.1; hazard ratio for distant disease or death, 0.57; 99.5% CI, 0.39 to 0.83; P<0.001).

Olaparib was associated with fewer deaths than placebo (59 and 86, respectively) (hazard ratio, 0.68; 99% CI, 0.44 to 1.05; P = 0.02); however, the between-group difference was not significant at an interim-analysis boundary of a P value of less than 0.01.

outcomes.analysisLabel: Second interim OS analysis (median follow-up 3.5 years)
outcomes.sourceQuote: With a median follow-up of 3.5 years, the second IA of OS demonstrated significant improvement in the olaparib group relative to the placebo group [hazard ratio 0.68; 98.5% confidence interval (CI) 0.47-0.97; P = 0.009]. Four-year OS was 89.8% in the olaparib group and 86.4% in the placebo group (Δ 3.4%, 95% CI -0.1% to 6.8%).

outcomes.analysisLabel: Second interim OS analysis (median follow-up 3.5 years)
outcomes.sourceQuote: Four-year IDFS for the olaparib group versus placebo group was 82.7% versus 75.4% (Δ 7.3%, 95% CI 3.0% to 11.5%) and 4-year DDFS was 86.5% versus 79.1% (Δ 7.4%, 95% CI 3.6% to 11.3%), respectively.

outcomes.analysisLabel: Second interim OS analysis (median follow-up 3.5 years)
outcomes.sourceQuote: Four-year IDFS for the olaparib group versus placebo group was 82.7% versus 75.4% (Δ 7.3%, 95% CI 3.0% to 11.5%) and 4-year DDFS was 86.5% versus 79.1% (Δ 7.4%, 95% CI 3.6% to 11.3%), respectively.

safety.sourceQuote: Safety data were consistent with known side effects of olaparib, with no excess serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest.
No new safety signals were identified including no new cases of acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome.

strengths: OS benefit demonstrated at second interim analysis
limitations: Interim analyses; maturity of long-term outcomes still accruing

clinicalImplications.text: Establishes 1 year of adjuvant olaparib for high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants, making germline testing relevant to adjuvant treatment planning.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Germline BRCA testing in high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer changes adjuvant therapy — order it early enough to inform post-chemotherapy decisions.
